source:
Game: Last Rogent (prototype)
Build a simple Roblox tower-defense / wave-survival game. A base sits at the end of a fixed path. Enemies spawn and walk the path toward the base. The player deploys and upgrades AI "agents" that fight the enemies. Survive escalating waves.
Core loop (this is the whole game for now):
 1. Prep - between waves, the player spends orbs (currency) to place or upgrade agents on fixed slots along the path.
 2. Fight - press "Start Wave." Enemies spawn and march the path. Placed agents auto-attack enemies in range. Enemies that reach the base deal damage to base health.
 3. Loot - killed enemies drop orbs. Orb count ticks up on screen.
 4. Repeat for the next, harder wave.
v1 scope - keep it minimal:
 • One agent type: place it on a slot, it auto-shoots the nearest enemy. Upgradable 1→2→3 (more damage / range each level).
 • One enemy type: walks the path, has HP, drops orbs on death, damages the base if it reaches the end.
 • 10 waves, each with more enemies and slightly more HP than the last.
 • Base health (e.g. 20). Hit 0 = game over. Survive wave 10 = win.
 • Simple UI: base health, current orb count, current wave number, and a "Start Wave" button.
Feel: fast, readable, satisfying. Orbs pop out of dead enemies. Placing/upgrading an agent is one tap on a slot. No menus, no accounts, no data saving yet - just the loop working in Play mode.
Start with a flat baseplate, a straight path of parts from a spawn point to the base, agent slots along the path, and get one wave fully working before adding the rest.

answers.ask: No visual theme was given beyond a grey baseplate prototype — should the finished map read as sci-fi, fantasy, or stylized toon?
answers.answer: Use a stylized toon prototype look: clean, colorful, highly readable shapes on the flat baseplate.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] theme — Q: No visual theme was given beyond a grey baseplate prototype — should the finished map read as sci-fi, fantasy, or stylized toon? A: Use a stylized toon prototype look: clean, colorful, highly readable shapes on the flat baseplate.
- [agent_inferred] scale — Q: How large should the minimal straight-path prototype be? A: Use one compact block-sized baseplate with a short readable lane and enough room for fixed agent slots on both sides.

## Enriched image prompt
Create a minimal stylized-toon tower-defense prototype on one flat baseplate. Run one straight, continuous path of clean colorful parts from a clearly marked enemy spawn mouth at one end to a visible core base at the other. Arrange a small set of fixed agent-placement slots evenly along both sides of the path, with enough clearance for placed agents to face the lane without overlapping it. Keep the ground flat, the silhouettes simple, and the spawn-to-base direction immediately readable. Do not add branches, extra lanes, raised terrain, shops, or decorative systems beyond the core prototype.

## Genre
The genre is Strategy, canonical slug `strategy`, because the game is a fixed-lane tower defense with deployable defenders and enemy waves attacking a base.

## Shape and preset
Use `lane-actor-track`, Path (Enemy Lane), for one continuous unchanging straight lane from wave origin to the core. The matched preset is Tower Defense, with its optional pinch point omitted to preserve the explicitly straight minimal path.

## Config requirements
Use `buildzone-grid` for the fixed agent-placement slots flanking both sides of the lane. Use the visible form of `tracker-core` for the core base at the terminal end. No `choke-bottleneck`, raised plateau, cover blocker, or additional route is grounded in the v1 scope.

## Layout requirements
Place one `spawner-npc` Spawner at the lane mouth, oriented toward the base. Place one `tracker-core` Tracker exactly at the terminal end of the path. The fixed placement slots are image geometry from `buildzone-grid`; keep each slot outside the enemy lane and give it a clear attack view toward the straight route.

## Layout components
The build contains one flat baseplate, one straight enemy path, one enemy spawn mouth, one terminal core base, and a small set of evenly spaced fixed agent slots on both sides. The baseplate edge forms the boundary. Compose the lane as a single unmistakable start-to-end axis with no branches or self-crossings.

## Render order
Use `topdown`: author the straight connected lane, terminal base, spawn mouth, and slot clearances first, then dress the plan in clean toon colors. The top-down plan is authoritative because any break in the lane would make enemy movement and the whole tower-defense loop fail.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
The scale is medium, the default block-sized band for a compact prototype where individual path parts and placement slots remain legible. The theme is a clean, colorful, highly readable stylized-toon prototype on a flat baseplate. Use `P6` because the enemy lane must be continuous and unambiguous by construction.
